summary.title: Game theory
bullets: Game theory studies strategic decisions where each player's outcome depends on the others' choices.
It is used in economics, politics and biology to model competition and cooperation.
Key ideas include dominant strategies, mixed strategies and equilibrium.
summary.quote: Game theory is the study of mathematical models of strategic interactions.

summary.title: Nash equilibrium explained
bullets: A Nash equilibrium is a set of strategies where no player gains by changing theirs alone.
John Nash proved every finite game has at least one equilibrium in mixed strategies.
The prisoner's dilemma is the classic case where equilibrium is not the best joint outcome.
summary.quote: No player can do better by unilaterally changing strategy.

summary.title: AI scribes in clinical documentation
bullets: Ambient AI scribes draft visit notes from the doctor-patient conversation.
Early pilots report less after-hours charting time for clinicians.
Accuracy review and patient consent remain open concerns.
summary.quote: Documentation burden is a leading driver of clinician burnout.

summary.title: Prior authorization reform and payers
bullets: Prior authorization requires approval from the payer before certain care is delivered.
New rules push payers toward faster, electronic decisions.
Providers still report delays and administrative cost.
summary.quote: Faster decisions depend on standardized electronic requests.

summary.title: FHIR and interoperability in hospitals
bullets: FHIR is a standard for exchanging health data through web APIs.
Hospitals adopt it to share records across systems.
Data quality and mapping remain the hard parts.
summary.quote: Interoperability is a data problem before it is a technology problem.

summary.title: How tool calling works in AI agents
bullets: The model chooses a tool and arguments from the tool descriptions it is given.
The application runs the tool and returns the result to the model.
Clear tool names and descriptions strongly affect selection accuracy.
summary.quote: Tool descriptions are the interface the model actually sees.

summary.title: Evaluating LLM applications
bullets: Start with a small set of real tasks and expected outcomes.
Score tool choice, arguments and failure handling separately.
Track cost and latency alongside accuracy.
summary.quote: You cannot improve what you do not measure.

summary.title: Deep work habits for product managers
bullets: Block long uninterrupted time for strategy and writing.
Batch meetings and messages into fixed windows.
Protect one planning ritual each week.

summary.title: Common OKR pitfalls
bullets: Too many objectives dilute focus.
Key results should measure outcomes, not activity.
Reviewing OKRs only quarterly hides drift.
summary.quote: A key result is a result, not a task.
